findings.body: Identical `rm -rf "${MISE_DATA_DIR}/installs/tiny/1"* 2>/dev/null || true` pattern as test_deps_tool_install: only deletes the compat symlink under the now-default identity layout, leaving the catalog-tracked install intact, so this regression test for the monorepo task install-order bug (discussions/9445) no longer reliably exercises the "tool not yet installed" path it's meant to guard.

`rm -rf "${MISE_DATA_DIR}/installs/tiny/1"* 2>/dev/null || true` only removes the compat symlink under the now-default identity layout; the real install + receipt survive, so resolver::locate() (catalog-first) still reports tiny@1 installed. This defeats the test's premise that tiny is uninstalled, undermining its dry-run assertions that tiny@1 needs installing. Same anti-pattern was fixed elsewhere in this branch via `mise uninstall`, but this file was missed.

default_enabled() makes the identity install layout apply to every backend (except the small is_exempt list) whenever experimental=true and install_layout is unset — previously this required the explicit install_layout="identity" opt-in. Because `experimental` is one global flag shared by unrelated features (monorepo, task artifact cache, dotfiles, etc.), any user/config enabling it for a different reason now gets hashed installs/<label>-<hash> paths instead of installs/<tool>/<version>. e2e/core/test_python_uv_venv_install sets MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1 (for uv venv auto-creation) without setting install_layout, and asserts `readlink .venv/bin/python` contains the literal `installs/python/3.12.3/` path; ToolVersion::install_path() (src/toolset/tool_version.rs:442-444) now returns the identity-layout hash directory for this tool, and plugins/core/python.rs's python_path() feeds that straight into uv's `--python` argument, so the venv's real interpreter path moves to `installs/python-<hash>/bin/python`. This test was not updated as part of the sweep, and the same hazard applies to any downstream tooling that hardcodes mise's conventional per-version paths after merely turning on an unrelated experimental feature. (Verified by code tracing only; could not build/run mise or the e2e suite in this environment.)
findings.statusReason: Fixed the concrete regression in 2d66716da: Python uv-venv and pipx binding tests now derive the selected interpreter and venv paths with mise where and verify the actual binding. Both Python e2e tests pass with experimental identity installs. The experimental default is the purpose of this PR; install_layout = legacy remains the documented opt-out. findings.body: In enabled(), the Some(other) arm for an unrecognized install_layout string (e.g. a typo of "legacy") now resolves via default_enabled(&settings), which returns true whenever experimental=true. The base branch instead always returned false for any non-"identity" value. Because install_layout is an unvalidated scalar String (no enum normalization in the settings codegen), a user who mistypes install_layout = "legacy" to opt out of the experimental identity layout, while experimental=true for an unrelated reason, will silently get the new identity layout instead of the legacy one they intended — the opposite of their configured intent. The new e2e test only covers a typo of "identity" (falls through to identity, matching intent), not this opt-out-failure direction.
findings.statusReason: Deliberate, after review on both sides of this: an unknown install_layout value is reported with a warning that names it, and is taken as unset, which keeps the default. Falling back to legacy instead would turn a misspelt "identity" into the opposite of its intent, the same problem in the other direction; the warning is what catches either typo.

findings.body: default_enabled() (resolver.rs:62) now turns on the identity install layout for any user with experimental=true and install_layout unset, not just explicit opt-ins. Under that layout, unlocked_choice() (resolver.rs:496-528) trusts a previously-recorded "selection" in the primary catalog even when the installation directory it names has since been relocated (e.g. moved into a directory added to MISE_SHARED_INSTALL_DIRS, a documented workflow per docs/mise-cookbook/docker.md): record_by_digest still finds the stale record, but is_complete() on the now-missing path is false, so locate() returns Located{installed:false} and never falls through to search roots()/shared dirs for the relocated copy (that search only runs on Unlocked::Nothing). mise then treats the tool as not installed (reinstall/exec failure) even though the data is present in a configured shared root. This exact failure was hit by this branch's own e2e/backend/test_vfox_rolling_install, which had to be patched to force MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=legacy for its initial install step — that workaround wasn't needed before this branch's default-on change, since identity layout previously required explicit opt-in and was never exercised by that test.
findings.statusReason: Deliberate: a selection is answered by what it names; a selected installation that is gone is not silently replaced by another copy (a primary one is restored in place on install). Moving an installation into a shared root by hand is followed by mise installs select <dir>, which the docs describe.

findings.body: Making install_layout default to "identity" whenever experimental=true (src/install_layout/resolver.rs enabled()/default_enabled()) newly exposes a latent resolver bug to ordinary experimental users: once a version's catalog selection is recorded in the primary store, moving its install directory into a MISE_SHARED_INSTALL_DIRS shared root (a supported workflow, e.g. for rolling/tracked versions) leaves the stale primary record in place. unlocked_choice's Selected branch only re-checks the recorded root, finds the directory gone, and reports installed:false instead of falling back to scan other roots the way Unlocked::Nothing/legacy_dir do — so mise treats the tool as not installed and reinstalls rather than reusing the shared copy. The PR's own e2e/backend/test_vfox_rolling_install had to be changed to `MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=legacy mise install` / `mise where` (lines 70-74) to sidestep this, with a comment describing exactly this failure, confirming it is real and still unresolved under the new default.

location.selectedText: /// The layout with `install_layout` unset: on with experimental features. Unit

findings.body: settings.toml (install_layout default) + src/install_layout/resolver.rs make the identity layout the default whenever experimental=true and install_layout is unset. e2e/run_test always exports MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1, so this branch flips the default layout for the whole e2e suite, not just the tests this PR touches. Under identity layout, `installs/<tool>/<version>` is only a compatibility symlink; the real installation is a catalog-tracked sibling `installs/<label>-<hash>` directory (src/install_layout/catalog.rs:182). This PR fixes ~20 e2e tests that used `rm -rf "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/<tool>"` to force a clean/reinstalled state by switching them to `mise uninstall --all` (e.g. e2e/cli/test_tool_depends, e2e/backend/test_github), but leaves the identical idiom unconverted in other files such as e2e/lockfile/test_multiple_version_constraints_lockfile (`rm -rf "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/tiny/1.1.0"` before re-`mise install`, meant to test lockfile-driven refetch), e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_tool_stub_sidecar (`rm -rf "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/aqua-jqlang-jq"` before testing MISE_LOCKED resolution without a lockfile), e2e/cli/test_install_task_tools, and e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_prefix. In each, the removal no longer deletes the real identity-layout installation, so mise's catalog resolves the still-present directory and the following `mise install` (without `--force`) just relinks rather than reinstalling — the assertions pass, but without exercising the "actually reinstalled from scratch" behavior the test was written to check, so a real regression in that code path could go undetected.
findings.statusReason: Fixed in e0a45327d and 466abad53: the remaining e2e tests that reinstall now uninstall through mise (npm aube lock, postinstall inline shell, task tools, jobs zero, multiple version constraints, lockfile install/prefix/provenance/aqua format, tool-stub sidecar). The rm -rf left in place run before anything is installed (fresh-env resets), or remove fake legacy directories the test made itself, or install with --force.

findings.body: enabled() now defaults identity-layout on whenever experimental=true and install_layout is unset (previously identity required the separate explicit opt-in). Since the real install payload lives in a sibling installs/<label>-<hash> directory, deleting installs/<tool> (or installs/<tool>/<version>, now just a compat link) no longer removes the installation — the next `mise install` silently reuses the surviving catalog entry. Any user who already has experimental=true set for an unrelated feature is switched onto this behavior with no warning, breaking the common 'rm -rf the tool dir to force a clean reinstall' idiom. The branch's own commits (8242a1f0c, 959b7e314) fixed this in ~20 e2e tests by switching to `mise uninstall`, but e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_tool_stub_sidecar:103 still does `rm -rf "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/aqua-jqlang-jq"` to assert no pre-installed jq satisfies a locked request without the lockfile — that assertion can now pass without actually removing jq's prior installation, so the test no longer reliably exercises the lockfile-driven resolution path it documents.
findings.statusReason: Test fixed in 466abad53: test_lockfile_tool_stub_sidecar uninstalls jq through mise and checks nothing is installed. Turning the layout on for experimental users is the intended step of this stack (jdx asked for it), and the docs describe uninstalling through mise rather than deleting installs/<tool>.

findings.body: The `Some(_) => true` pattern accepts any string value for `install_layout` (except "legacy"), including typos like "idenity" or arbitrary strings like "foo", when `experimental = true`. The settings.toml defines `enum = ["legacy", "identity"]` but the build-time validator only checks ListString/SetString types (build.rs:260), not plain String. A user who typos `install_layout = "idenity"` gets the identity layout silently enabled instead of an error. The previous branch rejected non-"identity" values (returned false). Change line 44 to `Some("identity") => true` to restore validation.
findings.statusReason: Fixed in 2714a2221: only "identity" turns the layout on; other values warn and keep the legacy layout.

findings.body: The match arm `Some(_) => true` at this location accepts any string value for install_layout except "legacy" when experimental=true. A user typo like `install_layout = "idenity"` or an arbitrary value like `install_layout = "foobar"` will silently enable the identity layout instead of being rejected. The enum constraint `["legacy", "identity"]` in settings.toml is not enforced at runtime for simple String types. The arm should explicitly match `Some("identity")` and reject unrecognized values.
findings.statusReason: Fixed in 2714a2221: only "identity" turns the layout on; any other value warns that it is neither identity nor legacy and keeps the legacy layout. e2e test_install_layout_experimental covers a misspelling.

findings.body: enabled() now matches `Some(_) => true` for any install_layout value that isn't literally "legacy" (e.g. a typo like "idenity", "Identity", or any other string) once experimental=true, because the install_layout enum (`["legacy","identity"]`) is never runtime-validated for this field — crates/mise-settings/build.rs only emits validate_setting_enum_values checks for ListString/SetString types, not plain String settings. Before this change, any value != "identity" (including such typos) unconditionally resolved to the legacy layout. Now a mistyped `install_layout` setting or `MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT` env value silently turns on the experimental identity install layout (new installs/<label>-<hash> directories, catalog, receipts) instead of being ignored, with no warning that the value was unrecognized — the existing warn_once! only fires when experimental is false, not when the string is simply invalid.
findings.statusReason: Fixed in 2714a2221: unknown install_layout values warn and keep the legacy layout instead of turning on the identity layout.

bodyDocument.textSnapshot:
Problem: The identity install layout—which names installations by their identity (backend, version, platform) rather than installs/<tool>/<version>—was opt-in even with experimental = true, requiring explicit install_layout = "identity" configuration. Users experimenting with other experimental features had to separately opt into the identity layout.
Solution: Make the identity layout the default behavior when experimental = true. Users who want to keep the legacy layout while using other experimental features can now set install_layout = "legacy" to opt out.
The branch updates the resolver logic so:
experimental = true with no layout setting → uses identity layout
install_layout = "legacy" → uses legacy layout (explicitly opts out, even with experimental enabled)
experimental = false → always uses legacy layout, regardless of layout setting
Unit tests still default to legacy to avoid side effects during test runs
Documentation and tests updated to reflect the new default, with legacy behavior explicitly enabled where needed. The feature still requires experimental = true; it cannot be used with stable settings.
